task_context.reference_solution:
From the angle addition formula,
\[1 = \tan 45^\circ = \tan (20^\circ + 25^\circ) = \frac{\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ}{1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ},\]so $\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ = 1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ.$

Then
\[(1 + \tan 20^\circ)(1 + \tan 25^\circ) = 1 + \tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ + \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ = \boxed{2}.\]

Okay, so $1 = (\tan 20 + \tan 25) / (1 - \tan 20 \tan 25)$. That means $\tan 20 + \tan 25 = 1 - \tan 20 \tan 25$. Now what? I have to simplify $(1 + \tan 20)(1 + \tan 25)$.

You're on the right track. Now, try expanding the original expression $(1 + \tan 20^\circ)(1 + \tan 25^\circ)$ using FOIL. Once you expand it, look for a way to substitute the relationship you just found.

If I expand it, I get $1 + \tan 20 + \tan 25 + \tan 20 \tan 25$. If I replace $\tan 20 + \tan 25$ with $1 - \tan 20 \tan 25$, it becomes $1 + (1 - \tan 20 \tan 25) + \tan 20 \tan 25$. Wait, the tan products cancel out! So it's just $1 + 1$. Is the answer 2?
